newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine Premier says backs central bank chief.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine Premier says backs central bank chief.

text.p: Ukrainian Prime Minister Pavlo Lazarenko said on Tuesday he would back the candidacy of central bank chief Viktor Yushchenko, who is seeking re-appointment from parliament.

"Central bank chief Mr Yushchenko has clear and concrete support from the government. There is and will be no other," Lazarenko told reporters after a meeting attended by President Leonid Kuchma and top industrial leaders.
Last week Kuchma asked deputies to grant a second, four-year term to Yushchenko, who is respected in the West as an advocate of tight monetary policy.
Lazarenko enjoys support among conservative leftists in parliament and his words could boost Yushchenko's chances of winning approval from a majority of deputies.
The deputy head of a parliamentary commission on finance and banking, Vadim Hetman, said parliament would not vote on Yushchenko's candidacy before mid-February.
Recently Lazarenko has criticised the bank's policies and accused commercial banks of not backing domestic producers.
